title: Cafe Society: the overloaded show and the two-piano boogie team
summary: Hammond got Turner and Pete Johnson into Barney Josephson's crowded show, which they played for about five years.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: He was puttin' in these shows with John. John Hammond was puttin' shows down at the Cafe Society. So he had, uh, Billie Holiday, Teddy Wilson, Hazel Scott, Lena Horne, Twelve Clouds...no, it wasn't the Twelve Clouds, it was, uh...the Golden Gate Quartet. They was all workin' in the... in Cafe Society...along with Meade Lux Lewis and Pete Joh...I mean, Albert Ammons. So the show was overloaded in the first place.

So...John Hammonds talked in...talked to Barney Josephson...put me and Pete Johnson in there. So I was pretty sharp. I was neat...cool. So, we went to work, an' me an' Billie Holiday used to get into a fight all the time.

She had the only dressing room. She had her private dressing room, and it was right near the steps as you go out the back way. So they had a...one of them old-time pianos with a mandolino attachment to it...self-player...used to be a self-player pianos--one o' them old-time pianos. So that's what, uh, Albert Ammons was playin' on ...Meade Lux Lewis. They play...they played single, and then they played together. Well, they playin' a boogie woogie. So me an' Pete Johnson showed up so they got used to usin' two pianos. Had a baby grand and this old piano together, and we...uh, got together with them and made a team out of it. Then we left. We played down there for about five years ...in the Village.

So, then, uh, Hazel Scott come out here to make a picture. Meantime, we had all the movie stars comin' down there...Mrs. Roosevelt ...Sophie Tucker...every big-time entertainer was in the business come down there.
